## Why visit

A specialist heritage option for travellers fascinated by the Manchester–Liverpool railway connection. The old rooms, screened service area and etched glass provide a substantial pub-history reason to visit, and its position beside Patricroft station connects the building to the journey between the two cities. The crucial limitation is current beer provision: it reopened after a closure but the latest CAMRA description explicitly says it no longer serves cask. Choose it for architecture and railway history, possibly alongside the Lamb, with that limitation understood.
